To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the coagulation and fibrosis processes are closely linked in acute inflammatory and fibrotic lung diseases and that the fibrinolytic system is a promising target for intervention in these diseases.

fibrin accumulation is a common feature in acute and chronic lung diseases and that fibrin itself can contribute to the inflammatory and fibrotic lung response by influencing the expression of inflammatory and profibrotic mediators and by providing an extracellular matrix for cell migration and proliferation.
fibrin deposition is a common feature of acute inflammatory and chronic fibrosing lung diseases.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of new therapeutic approaches in acute inflammatory and fibrotic lung diseases, which may be based on the inhibition of the procoagulatory and antifibrino-lytic state in the alveolar compartment of the lung.
a better understanding of the mechanisms of fibrin deposition in acute inflammatory and interstitial lung diseases in order to develop new therapeutic strategies.
the role of the coagulation system in lung diseases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the coagulation and antifibrino-lytic systems are not the only pathomechanisms involved in acute inflammatory and interstitial lung diseases but they are involved in a variety of processes that contribute to lung injury.
the alveolar haematosis and fibrinolytic system are important factors in acute and chronic lung diseases.
fibrin formation in acute inflammatory and interstitial lung diseases contributes to the pathogenesis and may represent an attractive therapeutic target.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the alveolar haematostatic system plays an important role in the pathophysiology of lung disease and that modulation of the haematostatic balance may represent an attractive therapeutic approach in the future.
alveolar coaulation and fibrinolytic systems are important factors in the pathogenesis of ARDS, acute interstitial lung disease and chronic interstitial fibrosing lung diseases.
the coagulation system is involved in the pathogenesis of ARDS, and that the coagulopathy of ARDS is not a consequence of the lung injury but a major cause for the development of the lung injury.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the coagulation and haemostatic systems play a major role in the development and progression of lung diseases and may be a potential target for therapeutic intervention.
fibrin deposition in ARDS and chronic interstitial pulmonary fibrosis may be a target for pharmacologic intervention.
a better understanding of the pathophysiological mechanisms underlying the coagulation-fibrinolytic imbalance may lead to the identification of novel targets for therapeutic intervention.
